A+ Custom Builders – Your Trusted Home Remodeling Contractor in Seekonk, MA

Welcome to A+ Custom Builders, your go-to home remodeling contractor serving Seekonk, Massachusetts, and the surrounding South Coast region. We specialize in custom renovations that enhance the comfort, function, and style of your home—from kitchens and bathrooms to basements, decks, and more.

With a reputation built on honest communication, expert craftsmanship, and a hands-on approach, we take pride in delivering results that exceed expectations—without outsourcing the work. When you choose A+, you’re hiring a skilled, in-house team that treats your home like their own.

HOME REMODELING SERVICES DESIGNED FOR YOU

As a full-service home remodeling contractor, we handle every aspect of your renovation with care and precision. Whether you're upgrading a single room or transforming your entire home, A+ Custom Builders is ready to bring your vision to life.

BATHROOM 

REMODELS

Bathroom Remodeling

Upgrade your bathroom into a spa-like retreat. We specialize in walk-in showers, modern vanities, tilework, and lighting that transforms your space from outdated to outstanding.

SHOW ME MORE

DECKS, PATIOS AND MORE

Decks & Outdoor Living Spaces

Enjoy the outdoors in style with a custom-built deck, patio, or pavilion. Our team builds outdoor spaces that are perfect for relaxing, entertaining, and making the most of New England’s changing seasons.

SHOW ME MORE

KITCHEN REMODELS

Kitchen Remodeling

We design and build kitchens that match your lifestyle and taste—from modern layouts with improved storage to full custom redesigns. Count on us to deliver a kitchen that's as functional as it is beautiful.

SHOW ME MORE

FINISHED BASEMENTS AND REMODELS

Basement Finishing

Turn your basement into a functional extension of your home. Whether you want a family room, gym, office, or guest suite, we create warm, livable spaces from the ground up.

SHOW ME MORE
WHY WORK WITH A+ CUSTOM BUILDERS?

When you're searching for a home remodeling contractor you can trust, it’s not just about the finished product—it’s about the process. At A+ Custom Builders, we make your experience as smooth and enjoyable as the final result.

Here’s what makes us different:

Transparent Estimates: Use our online calculator to get a ballpark price for your project before we even meet.

Tailored Design: Your project is one of a kind—and so is our approach. Every detail is built around your needs.

Respectful, Reliable Crew: We show up on time, keep your home clean, and deliver what we promise.

Proven Client Satisfaction: Our 5-star reviews speak for themselves. Homeowners choose us again and again for a reason.

HEAR FROM HAPPY CLIENTS

“A+ is the best home remodeling contractor we’ve worked with. Communication was top-notch and the quality of work is second to none.”
 — Joe L.

“They exceeded our expectations from start to finish. Every detail was thoughtfully executed.”
 — Laura B.

“We used A+ for a full basement remodel and couldn’t be happier. They do what they say—and they do it right.”
 — Richard F.

WHERE

Serving South Coast Massachusetts and  Rhode Island!

LET’S BRING YOUR VISION TO LIFE

Looking for a reliable, detail-driven home remodeling contractor in Seekonk or nearby? A+ Custom Builders is here to help. Whether you're ready to start now or just gathering ideas, we’ll guide you through every step of the remodeling process.

Your Trusted Bathroom Remodel Contractor

Looking to update your outdated bathroom? Partnering with a professional bathroom remodel contractor ensures your renovation is done right—from the tile work to the plumbing behind the walls. At A+ Custom Builders, we help homeowners throughout Seekonk, MA and the South Coast turn their bathrooms into beautiful, functional spaces they love.

Whether you're dreaming of a spa-inspired retreat or simply need a more efficient layout, our team delivers precision, quality, and peace of mind with every project.

WHY HIRE A BATHROOM REMODEL CONTRACTOR?

Bathrooms involve complex systems—plumbing, electrical, waterproofing—that leave no room for error. Hiring a licensed bathroom remodel contractor ensures your remodel meets code, stays on budget, and avoids costly mistakes.

Benefits of working with a pro:

Expert layout and design advice

Access to durable, high-quality materials

Coordination of all trades (plumbers, electricians, tile setters)

Faster timelines and fewer delays

Compliance with local building codes

FEATURED PROJECTS

HOMESTEAD CUSTOM BATHROOM 
HOMESTEAD GALLERY

Located in Rehoboth MA, this bathroom was actually not the main goal. An art studio was the main priority, the bathroom and master bedroom were in the way. Half the house was redesigned and reconfigured. The floor tile runs all the way up the vanity wall. Frosted window and door added to bring the natural light into the other rooms. By far our favorite room of the house! 

Homestead Project

LAWRENCE ST BATHROOM GALLERY
LAWRENCE ST BATHROOM RENOVATION

This bathroom in Swansea Massachusetts was just one portion of this homes renovation. Additional living space was added with an addition and a second floor dormer. The entire house from top to bottom was gutted and brought back to life! 

Lawrence St Project

PINE ST BATHROOM REMODEL 
PINE STREET BATHROOM

The addition of this brand new bathroom started with a new dormer in the front of this Rehoboth home. Click the link below to see more pictures. 

Pine Street Project

DILLON LN GALLERY
DILLON LANE BATH REMODEL

Located in the heart of Swansea this Master bath received some major love. 

Dillon Lan Project

EDGEWOOD 1/2 BATH REMODEL
EDGEWOOD GALLERY

When you love to host gatherings a guest bathroom is key. This Seekonk home is now ready to go!

Edgewood Project

PRICING
OUR STEP-BY-STEP REMODELING PROCESS

At A+ Custom Builders, we keep the remodeling process simple, smooth, and stress-free from start to finish.

STEP 1: PERSONALIZED CONSULTATION

We begin by learning your goals, style preferences, and budget. Whether you want to update a half-bath or fully renovate a master suite, we tailor every project to your needs.

STEP 2: SELECTIONS AND DESIGN

We help you choose tile, vanities, lighting, fixtures, and finishes that reflect your style and stand up to daily use.

STEP 3: PROFESSIONAL CONSTRUCTION

Once the plan is in place, our team gets to work. You can count on respectful crews, clear communication, and attention to every detail.

POPULAR BATHROOM REMODEL FEATURES

Today’s homeowners are looking for bathrooms that feel like a getaway and function like a dream. Some of the most requested upgrades include:

Walk-in tiled showers with glass enclosures

Double vanities for shared spaces

Heated tile floors for added comfort

Freestanding soaking tubs

Smart lighting and ventilation systems

Custom-built linen storage or shelving

According to the National Association of Realtors, bathroom remodels are one of the best ways to boost your home’s value, offering a typical return of around 70%.

WHAT SETS A+ CUSTOM BUILDERS APART

Not all contractors provide the same level of service. At A+ Custom Builders, we believe in earning your trust with honest communication, skilled craftsmanship, and a streamlined process.

When you choose us as your bathroom remodel contractor, you get:

Clear pricing with no surprises

Clean, professional crews that respect your home

Detailed timelines and reliable scheduling

Start Your Bathroom Renovation Today

If you're ready to create a bathroom that's beautiful, functional, and built to last, A+ Custom Builders is here to help. As a top-rated bathroom remodel contractor serving Seekonk and surrounding communities, we’re proud to deliver A+ results—every time.

Call 401-225-7875 today to schedule your consultation or get a free estimate.

GET YOUR FREE QUOTE

January 28, 2025
The Truth About Having Contractors in Your Home: It's Complicated, and That's OK

I want to talk about something we don't discuss enough in our industry – how it feels to have contractors in your home.

Your home isn't just a house. It's where your kids do their homework, where you enjoy Sunday morning coffee, where you unwind after a long day. It's your sanctuary.

And let's be honest – having contractors there changes that feeling. Even with the best team, it's an adjustment. As a homeowner myself, I get it.

Even with the most seasoned, professional contractor, home improvements and repairs are inherently inconvenient. Understanding this reality is the first step toward a better experience.

ACKNOWLEDGING THE ELEPHANT IN THE ROOM

Your home is your sanctuary, and having it transformed into a construction zone is stressful. There will be noise. Your routine will be disrupted. Your privacy will feel compromised. These aren't just minor inconveniences – they're legitimate concerns that deserve acknowledgment.

THE PERFECT CONTRACTOR…

If only finding the "perfect contractor" will eliminate all of our anxieties. While choosing the right contractor is crucial, even the best can't completely eliminate the inherent disruptions of home improvement projects. What they can do is:

Serve you how you want to be served.

Create clear expectations about timelines, daily work schedules, and potential challenges, helping you mentally prepare for the experience rather than being blindsided by surprises.

Establish open and honest communication channels and regular check-ins, ensuring you never feel left in the dark and are always aware of what is happening in your home and the next steps. 

Demonstrate respect for your space through simple but meaningful actions like protecting furniture, having a dust control plan, wearing boot covers, and cleaning up thoroughly at the end of each day.

BUILDING TRUST THROUGH TRANSPARENCY

The most trustworthy contractors aren't the ones who promise a perfectly smooth experience – they're the ones who are honest about the challenges while showing how they'll help you navigate them. Look for contractors who:

Have a clear process, starting with the sales process all the way to how they close out the job. 

Provide detailed, written proposals

Share references freely and encourage you to contact their previous clients

Maintain appropriate licensing, insurance, and certifications for their work

THE HUMAN ELEMENT

Will Guidara says “The best service experiences aren't about perfection – they're about genuine human connection and care”  A great contractor understands this by:

Taking time to learn about your family's specific needs and concerns

Adapting their work schedule to accommodate your important daily routines when possible

Introducing you to all team members who will be working in your home

Showing genuine enthusiasm for helping you achieve your vision

Looking for ways throughout the project to make things easier and more enjoyable for you

MAKING PEACE WITH THE PROCESS

Instead of hoping for a perfectly smooth experience, focus on finding a contractor who will be a genuine partner in navigating the inevitable challenges. The right professional will:

Validate your concerns rather than dismissing them

Proactively solve problems before they escalate

Keep you informed about progress and setbacks alike

Show genuine care for your home and family throughout the project

THE SILVER LINING

While having contractors in your home will never be entirely convenient, the right approach can make it significantly more bearable. By acknowledging the challenges upfront and focusing on building a trusting relationship with your contractor, you can shift your perspective from dreading the process to appreciating the transformation of your space.

Remember, at the end of the project, the disruption is temporary, but the improvements to your home will last for years to come. The key is not to seek the perfect experience, but to find a contractor who will treat your home with respect, your concerns with understanding, and your project with dedication.

September 6, 2022
What is the difference between an Estimate and a Proposal?
ESTIMATES VS PROPOSALS AND WHY YOU NEED BOTH!

By Greg DeSilva

     An estimate is an educated guess of cost, while a proposal is a detailed contract with an exact cost.  At first glance you might think “I definitely want a proposal then, what good is an estimate?”  An estimate has its time and place and should never be skipped! It should always come first to save you time and aggravation as a home owner as well as for a contractor. When estimates are skipped, which happens often as most contractors offer “free estimates” and don’t realize they’re actually giving out proposals,  it wastes everyone’s time if the contractor does not get that particular job. By getting/giving estimates you can see if your budget is in the same ball park of the estimated cost. For example: If a homeowner thinks a master bathroom can be done for $10,000 while most master bathrooms start at $30,000 today in our area, then that conversation should be a short over the phone educational conversation. It should not be a 1/2 hour drive to the home, 45 minutes in the home, 1/2 hour drive back to the office, 45 minutes drawing up a proposal/contract and sending it over just to find out the budget was 1/3 the actual cost. Also as a homeowner, researching contractors, calling a number of contractors, setting up times to be home to meet them, waiting for the appointment, waiting for the “proposal” etc. would be a waste of time and energy. When estimates and proposals are understood and used properly it benefits both parties. 

June 23, 2022
How long will my bathroom remodel take?

A bathroom remodel can take anywhere from 4 to 8 weeks. The size of the remodel will dictate the timeline.

Although the smallest room in the house, the bathroom can be a lengthy renovation due to the different trades involved that all require their own inspections.  Electricians, carpenters, plumbers, tile setters, drywallers, painters etc…

Each task and trade can take a few days and then you have to account for inspections from your local inspector (some take longer than others). Also take into account that most contractors do not have in house electricians and plumbers on their payroll so there most likely will be schedule conflicts as well. 

The process:        Demo, framing, rough plumbing then inspection, rough electrical then inspection, framing inspection, insulation inspection, drywall/plaster, tub/shower/tile, painting, vanity install, mirrors and accessories, final plumbing, final electrical, then 3 final inspections. 

HIRING A BATHROOM REMODELER!

When hiring, focus less on a start date and more on the deadline. This will make the project go much smoother in my experience by adding accountability. Ask about subcontractors and who will be in your home and how long they have been working together. Make sure to express any concerns you may have! For example, if dust is a problem for you and your family or you’re worried about someone letting the dog out by accident or your floors were just re-done and you want to make sure they are protected. These small things often get overlooked but are the most important. Bottom line is to find someone you can trust and get a long with. Any renovation can be a great experience if you choose the right people. Hire the person that’s a better listener than talker. Your wants and needs should be their main concern!

February 28, 2022
The Rich Peoples Tax

Written by Greg DeSilva 

     What is the “Rich Peoples Tax” ? Its when you call a contractor for lets say central air in your 1700 square foot house. You have the one unit installed for the price of X.  A few years down the road you have done well financially, and now have been able to live in a much bigger home, lets say 6,000 square feet. This home has basically the same central air units as your previous home, but has 3 of them. So you call a contractor to come take a look. They come by and see your new range rover next to your wife’s or husband’s Mercedes in the the driveway, and check out the beautiful $6,000 square foot house you’ve worked so hard for. That same A/C unit now costs 10X, and you have 3 of them. That’s what I mean when I say “Rich People’s Tax”.

   I have been judged in my life a time or two. Its not fun when you notice it, and frankly it is not right in my opinion.  So, what good is this information? other than telling that things will cost you more now? Well, did you know some contractors are actually trustworthy… Some even put their pricing right on their websites to earn your trust and be transparent.  Take the time to look for those that do, I can assure you, they are most likely the best to work with.

Common questions from Lake County homeowners about remodeling projects

How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Lake County, IL?

Kitchen remodel costs in Lake County vary based on size, materials, and scope. A moderate kitchen renovation typically ranges from $25,000 to $75,000, while larger projects with custom cabinetry and high-end finishes can run higher. We provide free, detailed estimates so you know exactly what to expect before any work begins.

Do I need a permit for a remodeling project in Lake County?

Most structural work, electrical, plumbing, and additions require permits in Lake County municipalities like Grayslake, Libertyville, and Mundelein. Our team handles the permitting process for you, ensuring your project meets all local building codes and passes inspection the first time.

How long does a bathroom remodel take?

A typical bathroom remodel in our experience takes 2 to 4 weeks depending on the scope — whether it involves new tile work, plumbing relocation, or a full gut renovation. We keep you informed with clear timelines and regular communication throughout the project.

Do you offer free estimates for remodeling projects?

Yes! We offer free in-person estimates for homeowners in Lake County and the surrounding area, including Lindenhurst, Vernon Hills, Gurnee, Buffalo Grove, and beyond. We’ll walk through your project on-site so you get an accurate, no-pressure quote.

What areas in Lake County do you serve?

We serve homeowners within about a 20-mile radius of Lindenhurst, IL. That includes Grayslake, Libertyville, Mundelein, Vernon Hills, Gurnee, Barrington, Long Grove, Buffalo Grove, Lincolnshire, Lake Forest, Deerfield, Highland Park, Northbrook, Waukegan, and many more Lake County communities.

Can you help with room additions, garages, and deck construction?

Absolutely. In addition to interior remodeling, we build room additions, garages, decks, and handle exterior projects like painting and siding throughout Lake County. From planning and permits to the final walkthrough, we manage every detail of your project.

How is Rohrer for Construction different from other Lake County contractors?

We’ve been serving Lake County since 1989. Unlike companies that subcontract everything, the majority of our work is done in-house by our own experienced crew. That means better quality control, clearer communication, and a team that’s worked together for over 35 years. We’re licensed, insured, bonded, BBB accredited, and carry a 4.9-star review average.

Rohrer for Construction was founded by Adolph Rohrer with the goal of providing honest, high-quality remodeling services to homeowners in Lake County. Over time, that local reputation grew through steady work, strong relationships, and a commitment to craftsmanship that homeowners could trust.

LAKE COUNTY, IL GENERAL CONTRACTOR

General Contractor Services in Lake County, IL

Rohrer for Construction helps homeowners across Lake County, Illinois manage remodeling, renovation, repair, and specialty home improvement projects with one trusted contractor overseeing the process from start to finish.

Whether you are planning a kitchen remodel, bathroom renovation, basement finishing project, exterior improvement, garage build, or a larger mixed-scope home project, our team helps bring structure, communication, and accountability to the work.

RESIDENTIAL GENERAL CONTRACTING

One Contractor Managing the Bigger Picture

Hiring a general contractor is about more than finding someone to perform labor. It is about working with a company that can help organize the project, coordinate the moving parts, communicate clearly, and keep the work progressing in the right direction. At Rohrer for Construction, we help homeowners simplify that process by bringing project oversight under one roof.

Many remodeling and home improvement projects involve more complexity than they appear to at first. A kitchen may involve cabinetry, plumbing, electrical, flooring, trim, paint, and finish coordination. A bathroom remodel may involve demolition, tile work, waterproofing, fixture placement, ventilation, and final detailing. A basement, exterior, or garage project can introduce structural considerations, specialty materials, and site-related work that need to be handled in the right order.

As a general contractor in Lake County, IL, we help homeowners move those projects forward with a more organized process. Our work regularly includes kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, basement finishing and remodeling, exterior remodeling, custom residential improvements, and broader home renovation work throughout Lake County.

Why homeowners choose a general contractor
One team managing scheduling and project flow
Better communication during remodeling and construction
Less stress when multiple phases of work are involved
Clearer accountability from start to finish
Better coordination across larger or more detailed projects
A smoother path from idea to completed result
General Contractor Services for Every Stage of Home Improvement

Some homeowners come to us for a single-room remodel. Others need broader help with structural, exterior, lower-level, or mixed-scope projects. We approach each job with the same goal: help the homeowner move the work forward with better planning and better oversight.

01
Interior Remodeling

Kitchens, bathrooms, and other interior projects that benefit from detailed planning, sequencing, and finish coordination.

02
Exterior & Structural Work

Entry improvements, framing, covered structures, garages, and exterior projects that require a more complete construction approach.

03
Custom & Mixed-Scope Projects

Specialty home improvements and larger residential projects that do not fit into a single standard service category.

KITCHEN REMODELING

Kitchen Remodeling With Better Coordination From Start to Finish

Kitchen remodeling is one of the most common reasons homeowners look for a general contractor near them. A kitchen project often includes cabinet planning, countertop coordination, lighting, flooring, plumbing, electrical work, trim, paint, and finish sequencing. Even when the final space feels clean and effortless, the work behind it usually requires careful management.

Rohrer for Construction helps homeowners approach kitchen projects with a practical process and a focus on how the finished space will actually function day to day. If your project is centered around your kitchen, visit our Kitchen Remodeling in Lake County, IL page for more kitchen-specific details.

Explore Kitchen Remodeling

BATHROOM REMODELING

Bathroom Remodeling That Balances Beauty, Durability, and Daily Use

Bathroom remodeling takes precision. Layout decisions, waterproofing, tile work, plumbing fixtures, ventilation, lighting, storage, and finish details all matter. Homeowners are not just updating appearance, they are improving one of the most heavily used spaces in the home.

We help homeowners plan bathroom remodeling work with long-term use in mind. If your project is bathroom-focused, our Bathroom Remodeling in Lake County, IL page goes deeper into the service.

See Bathroom Remodeling Options
More Residential General Contractor Services

General contracting often means helping homeowners with projects that extend beyond a single room. We work on basements, exteriors, garages, custom spaces, structural improvements, and specialty home upgrades throughout Lake County.

LOWER-LEVEL LIVING SPACE

Basement Finishing & Remodeling

Basement remodeling can create useful, comfortable space for family living, entertaining, work, hobbies, or storage. Lower-level projects often involve layout planning, moisture awareness, finish materials, lighting, and design decisions that shape how the space feels once completed.

Learn more on our Basement Finishing & Remodeling in Lake County, IL page.

Learn About Basement Remodeling

CUSTOM RESIDENTIAL FEATURES

Saunas, Specialty Spaces, and Unique Projects

Some homeowners want something more tailored than a standard remodel. We also work on custom spaces, specialty residential features, and projects that do not fit neatly into a cookie-cutter service category.

That kind of work is a good fit for our broader Additional Services offering.

View Additional Services

EXTERIOR IMPROVEMENTS

Exterior Remodeling

Exterior work can improve curb appeal, entry function, weather protection, and the overall appearance of the home. Covered entries, trim details, exterior updates, and broader exterior renovations often benefit from contractor-led planning and execution.

View Exterior Remodeling Services

OUTDOOR LIVING & SPECIALTY STRUCTURES

Screen Houses, Covered Spaces, and Custom Exterior Features

Outdoor living structures and custom exterior additions can make a home more usable and enjoyable. Projects like these often involve framing, roofing details, finish work, and design considerations that require stronger coordination than a basic repair.

See Additional Service Options

GARAGES AND STRUCTURAL WORK

Garage Construction and Framing Projects

Some homeowners need more than interior remodeling. Garage-related construction, framing, and structural work call for a contractor who can think beyond finishes and account for the full flow of the build.

If your project includes larger construction elements, reach out through our contact page so we can talk through the scope.

Talk With Us About Your Project

SITE PREPARATION & PROJECT SUPPORT

Digging, Prep Work, and Construction Support

Some projects begin with site work and structural preparation rather than finishes. Digging, post holes, and construction prep matter because what happens early in the project affects everything that comes after.

Ask About Your Project
Project Highlights Across Kitchens, Bathrooms, Basements, and More

As a home remodeling contractor in Lake County, IL, we work across multiple areas of the home. These photos reflect the range of projects we help homeowners manage, from interior upgrades to broader home improvements.

SMALLER PROJECTS AND REPAIRS

Not Every Home Project Needs Full General Contracting

Some jobs are simply smaller in scale. If the work is repair-based, maintenance-focused, or does not require the coordination that comes with a larger remodel, our Rohrer Handyman Services division may be the better fit.

That gives homeowners a more practical option for smaller projects while keeping full general contracting reserved for projects that truly need that level of management.

Visit Rohrer Handyman Services
How Our General Contractor Process Works

Every project is different, but homeowners almost always benefit from a clearer path forward. Our process is built around communication, coordination, and helping the project stay organized as it moves from concept to completion.

01
Initial Conversation

We learn about your home, your goals, and the kind of remodeling or improvement work you are considering.

02
Scope Review

We talk through the project direction and help determine the right approach for the work ahead.

03
Planning & Coordination

We organize the project flow, moving parts, and next steps so the job starts with structure.

04
Construction Oversight

The work is managed with communication, accountability, and attention to the bigger picture.

05
Completion

We work toward a finished result that supports the homeowner’s goals, budget, and long-term use of the space.

SERVING LAKE COUNTY, IL

General Contractor Services Throughout the Area

Rohrer for Construction works with homeowners throughout Lake County, including Lindenhurst, Gurnee, Grayslake, Libertyville, Antioch, Round Lake, Round Lake Beach, Wauconda, Fox Lake, and nearby communities.

If you are searching for a general contractor near me, a local general contractor in Lake County, IL, or a company that can help coordinate your remodeling project from start to finish, we are ready to talk through your goals.

Experience a Bathroom Remodel That Exceeds Expectations in Lake County, IL

Your bathroom isn't just a utilitarian space; it's a sanctuary, a private retreat where you start and end your day. If your current bathroom feels outdated, cramped, or simply doesn't meet your needs, it's time to consider a professional bathroom remodel. At Rohrer for Construction, we've been helping homeowners across Lake County, from Antioch to Waukegan, redefine their living spaces since 1989. Our dedication to superior craftsmanship and client satisfaction ensures your new bathroom will be a perfect blend of aesthetic appeal and optimal functionality.

We understand that a bathroom renovation is a significant investment. That's why our approach is built on transparency, meticulous planning, and open communication. From selecting durable, stylish materials like Delta faucets and Schluter waterproofing systems to optimizing layouts for maximum space and accessibility, our crew handles every technical detail with expert precision. You'll work directly with Adolph and Austin Rohrer, ensuring a personal touch and accountability from start to finish. Let's transform your vision into a tangible, beautiful reality.

Unlock Comfort and Value with a Strategic Bathroom Remodel

Many homeowners in Lake County consider a bathroom remodel for various reasons, but the core motivation often boils down to two things: enhancing daily comfort and increasing home value. A well-executed bathroom renovation can drastically improve your quality of life, offering a refreshed, more efficient, and aesthetically pleasing space. Imagine starting your day in a bright, modern bathroom with heated floors and a spacious walk-in shower, or unwinding in a beautifully designed sanctuary after a long day.

Beyond personal enjoyment, a bathroom remodel offers one of the best returns on investment (ROI) in home renovation. Understanding Bathroom Remodel Pricing Factors in Lake County

A simple cosmetic update, like new paint and vanity, will naturally cost less than a full renovation involving layout changes, plumbing relocation, or structural modifications. Moving walls or reconfiguring the shower and toilet typically incurs higher labor and material costs due to additional plumbing, electrical work, and permitting requirements.

From entry-level ceramic tiles to high-end natural stone or large-format porcelain, and from standard laminate countertops to quartz or granite, material choices significantly impact the budget. Permits & Inspections

Customization & Features

Exploring Essential Materials and Options for Your Lake County Bathroom

The longevity and aesthetic of your bathroom remodel heavily depend on the materials you choose. In Lake County, where homes experience diverse weather patterns, selecting durable and moisture-resistant materials is paramount. We guide our clients through a curated selection of options, ensuring both beauty and resilience.

Flooring: Tile, LVT, and More

Porcelain and Ceramic Tile: These are classic choices for their water resistance, durability, and wide range of styles. Porcelain, being less porous, is excellent for high-moisture areas. Brands like Daltile and Marazzi offer extensive collections.

Luxury Vinyl Tile (LVT): A fantastic option for its waterproof properties, warmth underfoot, and ability to mimic wood or stone at a more accessible price point. Ideal for homeowners seeking both practicality and style.

Countertops: Quartz, Granite, and Solid Surface

Quartz: Engineered stone offering exceptional durability, stain resistance, and a non-porous surface, making it highly hygienic. Comes in a vast array of colors and patterns, including options that resemble natural stone.

Granite: A natural stone known for its unique patterns and strength. Requires periodic sealing but offers unparalleled elegance and heat resistance. Both are popular in upscale Lake County remodels.

Fixtures: Faucets, Showers, Toilets

Faucets & Shower Systems: We recommend trusted brands like Delta, Kohler, and Moen for their reliability, water efficiency, and design versatility. Options include thermostatic valves for precise temperature control and low-flow fixtures for water conservation.

Toilets: Comfort-height and dual-flush models are popular for both accessibility and water efficiency. Brands like Toto and American Standard lead the market in performance and design.

Waterproofing & Backer Board

Schluter Systems: For showers, we often utilize advanced waterproofing systems like Schluter-Kerdi. This integrated system ensures complete moisture management, preventing leaks and mold growth, which is critical in humid bathroom environments.

Cement Board: Provides a stable, water-resistant base for tiling walls and floors, superior to standard drywall in wet areas. Proper installation is key to preventing long-term issues.

Shower Enclosure Installation

A shower enclosure should fit the opening, contain water, and feel right to use every day. Rohrer for Construction coordinates shower enclosure installation as part of bathroom remodeling, from reviewing the shower area and selecting a door style to arranging installation and finishing details. We are a family-owned general contractor serving Lake County since 1989. Homeowners in Gurnee can request a free estimate to discuss a new enclosure or a larger bathroom update.

Request a Free Estimate
See Our Projects
Written by Rohrer for Construction | Serving Lake County, IL since 1989 —
Last reviewed/Updated: October 2026
What shower enclosure installation includes

A well-planned enclosure is more than a glass panel or door. The opening must be measured, the shower walls and curb checked, and the enclosure style matched to how the bathroom is laid out. We review the existing conditions and discuss how the door will open, where water may reach, and how the finished enclosure will work with the rest of the room.

The project scope can include removing an existing enclosure, preparing the surrounding area, coordinating the glass and hardware, installing the selected enclosure, and completing related finish work. If the shower itself needs updating, we can plan the enclosure alongside tile, plumbing, or other bathroom remodeling work. Explore our bathroom remodeling services to see how a shower upgrade can fit into a broader project.

An enclosure replacement may be a focused improvement, while a remodel may be appropriate when the shower base, walls, or layout also need attention. We will clarify what is included in the project plan so you can make decisions based on the condition of your bathroom and the result you want.

Review of the shower opening, surrounding surfaces, and access
Planning for door movement, entry clearance, and hardware placement
Coordination of enclosure installation with related bathroom work
Finish details that help the enclosure work with the room
Choose an enclosure style and materials that suit the space

The right enclosure depends on the shower’s dimensions and the room around it. A sliding door can be useful where a hinged door would interfere with a vanity, toilet, or walkway. A hinged door needs enough clear floor area to swing open comfortably. Fixed glass panels can create an open feel, while a framed or semi-frameless design can provide a more defined edge around the glass.

Glass appearance, framing, hardware finish, and door configuration all affect the finished look. Clear glass keeps the tile visible; other glass treatments can offer more visual privacy. Frame and hardware choices can complement existing fixtures or be selected as part of a bathroom refresh. We help you compare practical options against the shape of the shower and the style of the room rather than choosing by appearance alone.

The surface behind the enclosure matters, too. Tile joints, curb shape, wall alignment, and the shower base influence how the enclosure can be fitted. In older Lake County homes—including ranches, split-levels, and colonials built from the 1950s through the 1990s—bathroom layouts and existing finishes can vary. We assess the actual opening before finalizing the plan, rather than assuming that a standard enclosure will fit.

Sliding, hinged, and fixed-panel configurations
Clear or privacy-oriented glass options
Framed or less visually prominent frame designs
Hardware finishes selected to coordinate with bathroom fixtures
When it is time to replace or add an enclosure

A shower door that no longer closes properly, glass that is damaged, or water escaping onto the bathroom floor are reasons to have the enclosure assessed. Changes to the bathroom—such as replacing the shower base, updating wall tile, or converting an older tub area—can also make a new enclosure part of the work. A door that blocks a walkway or conflicts with nearby fixtures may be a sign that a different configuration deserves consideration.

An enclosure alone may not address water that is getting behind tile or through a failed shower base. If the surrounding area shows persistent dampness, loose finishes, or damage, the underlying cause should be evaluated before new glass is installed. We can discuss whether the project is limited to the enclosure or should include related shower or bathroom work.

Winter freeze-thaw conditions in northern Illinois make sound exterior construction important, but the enclosure itself is an interior fixture. For bathrooms, the focus is on proper fit, sound surrounding surfaces, and keeping routine shower water within the intended wet area. Hard well or municipal water can leave mineral deposits on glass and hardware, so consider cleaning and upkeep when comparing glass and finish options.

Permits and local coordination

A straightforward enclosure replacement may not involve the same approvals as a bathroom remodel that changes plumbing, electrical work, or the room’s structure. Permit requirements depend on the work and the authority responsible for the property. In Lake County, local review requirements can differ, so it is best to confirm them before construction begins.

Rohrer handles permit applications when they are required for the agreed project scope and coordinates the related approval steps. We identify permit considerations during planning, before work starts. For background, see our building permit guidance and the county’s Lake County building permit information. The correct permitting authority depends on the property and project; the county resource is useful for checking where to begin.

A local contractor for a carefully planned bathroom project

Rohrer for Construction has served Lake County since 1989 as a family-owned general contractor. We can coordinate the enclosure with other parts of a bathroom project, help identify decisions that need to be made before installation, and handle permits when the work requires them. That matters when a glass update is one part of a larger renovation and several trades or finish choices need to line up.

Our planning focuses on the existing bathroom, the changes you want, and the work needed to complete them. Learn more about Rohrer and our local contracting approach, or use our scope builder to prepare for a conversation about your project. We will discuss the next steps and provide a free estimate based on the work involved.

What walk-in shower installation includes

A walk-in shower project can involve more than removing a tub and setting a new shower in its place. We assess the existing layout, plumbing, wall and floor conditions, access, and ventilation, then plan the enclosure and finishes to suit the room. Work may include demolition, preparation of the shower base and walls, waterproofing, tile or other wall finishes, plumbing fixtures, glass, and final trim.

The scope depends on the bathroom. Keeping the shower near existing plumbing can make the plan more straightforward; changing the drain location, moving plumbing, or adjusting walls may require additional coordination. We review these decisions during planning and explain the proposed scope before construction. Explore our bathroom remodeling services for broader project options.

Shower base and entry: choose a curb or discuss a low-threshold design suited to the room and project.
Wall finishes: compare ceramic or porcelain tile with other suitable shower-wall systems.
Storage and support: plan niches, shelves, a built-in bench, or grab-bar blocking where appropriate.
Enclosure and fixtures: consider a fixed glass panel or door, showerhead style, and control placement.
Choose materials and features for everyday use

Tile offers flexibility in color, pattern, and size. Porcelain and ceramic are common choices for shower walls and floors, while smaller floor tiles can provide more grout lines for traction. Grout selection and upkeep matter, too. Large-format tile creates a different look and has different installation requirements than mosaic tile; the shower floor and slope need to work with the selected material and drain.

A shower with a bench can make bathing more comfortable, but its dimensions and placement should preserve usable standing space and access to controls. A built-in niche keeps bottles off the floor, and glass can help maintain an open sightline. We help you weigh these choices against the room’s footprint, cleaning preferences, and the needs of household members. For ideas across a complete project, visit our completed project portfolio.

Select slip-conscious floor materials and a layout that suits the shower base.
Coordinate tile, grout, glass hardware, and plumbing finishes before installation.
Consider a handheld showerhead, bench, or support features as part of the plan.
Allow for ventilation and accessible cleaning around glass, corners, and niches.

When a walk-in shower may be the right choice

Homeowners often consider a walk-in shower when a tub is rarely used, stepping over a high tub wall has become difficult, or an older enclosure shows wear. A remodel can also address cracked or dated finishes, inconvenient controls, limited storage, and water concerns. If you are planning around aging in place, discuss entry height, seating, clearances, and future support needs early; the best arrangement depends on the room and the people using it.

Many local homes, including 1950s–1990s ranches, split-levels, and colonials, have bathrooms where the existing footprint guides what can be changed. Freeze-thaw winters make sound waterproofing and careful construction important: water that reaches surrounding materials can cause damage over time. We inspect the existing conditions and plan the shower assembly as part of the full scope rather than treating tile as the only decision.

If you are deciding between keeping a tub and replacing it with a shower, our bathroom remodeling page offers a starting point for discussing the room as a whole.

Changes to plumbing or other building systems can affect what applications and inspections are needed, and requirements may differ between a village and unincorporated areas. We review the project details, coordinate applicable permit applications, and plan for required inspections before work proceeds.

A shower remodel may affect the bathroom while demolition and installation are underway, so we discuss access and practical preparation as part of planning. The aim is to make decisions in advance and keep the work aligned with the agreed scope.

Many local homes built from the 1950s through the 1990s have bathrooms sized around a standard tub or a compact shower. Choose a shower layout and materials for daily use

A walk-in shower can use a curb or a low-threshold entry. A curbless design may make entry easier, but it requires careful coordination of floor height, drainage, and waterproofing; it is not suitable for every existing bathroom. We review the available space and conditions before settling on a plan. A hinged or sliding glass enclosure can help define the wet area, while a fixed panel may suit some open layouts.

Wall finishes can include tile or shower-rated panel systems. Tile offers choices in color, format, and pattern, but needs properly detailed waterproofing and grout maintenance. Panels reduce grout lines and create a more continuous surface. For the floor, the shower base and drain must work together; a tiled shower floor needs a suitable pitch and a surface selected with footing in mind. We can discuss practical tradeoffs as you choose finishes.

Think through storage and fixtures early. Recessed niches, corner shelves, a handheld shower, and a comfortable control location can make the space work better without changing the overall footprint. If you are comparing shower choices with the rest of a bathroom project, our bathroom remodeling overview is a useful place to start.

Compare tile with shower-rated panels for appearance and cleaning preferences.

A shower remodel is worth considering when access has become difficult, a household’s needs have changed, or an old enclosure no longer fits your routine. A wider opening, a handheld shower, well-placed controls, and a bench may support easier use. Their fit depends on the room dimensions and the way water will be contained, so those details should be resolved before construction begins.

Freeze-thaw winters are part of life in this area, but the shower itself depends most on sound water management indoors: intact waterproofing, careful transitions, and a properly installed drain. Hard water from a well or municipal supply can also leave mineral deposits on glass and fixtures. Choosing finishes that suit your cleaning habits and using routine care can help keep the new shower presentable.

In Holiday Hills, in McHenry County, and Lakemoor, in Lake County, permit requirements can depend on the project scope and the authority responsible for the property. Changes to plumbing or electrical work may trigger review or inspections. We check applicable requirements and handle permits when needed rather than asking you to guess which forms apply. Bathtub Replacement

BATHROOM REMODELING BY A LOCAL CONTRACTOR SINCE 1989

Bathtub Replacement

A worn, cracked, or hard-to-clean tub can make an otherwise useful bathroom frustrating. Rohrer for Construction replaces bathtubs as part of a planned bathroom remodel, helping you choose a tub and surround that suit your space, daily routine, and maintenance preferences. We serve homeowners in Lake County and nearby McHenry County, handle required permits, and invite you to request a free estimate.

Request a Free Estimate
See Our Projects
Written by Rohrer for Construction | Serving Lake County, IL since 1989 —
Last reviewed/Updated: October 2026
A better fit for the way you use your bathroom

Bathtub replacement can be a focused update or part of a broader bathroom remodel. The work may include removing the old tub, preparing the surrounding area, setting the replacement, installing a new surround or tile, and finishing adjoining surfaces. The right scope depends on the room’s condition and whether you want to keep the existing layout.

Some homeowners want a fresh tub for bathing children or soaking. Others want easier entry or prefer to replace a tub with a walk-in shower. If you are considering a conversion, we can discuss the room layout and options for shower enclosure installation. The drain, water protection, shower base, and enclosure need to be planned together.

Many Lake County homes built from the 1950s through the 1990s have ranch, split-level, or colonial layouts with compact bathrooms. We look at room dimensions, doorway access, plumbing location, storage, and how the tub meets adjoining walls. Keeping the tub in its current location may limit plumbing changes. Moving it can add work to the project.

Choose a tub, surround, and finish that work together

Bathtubs come in different shapes, depths, and materials. Acrylic is a lighter-weight option with a smooth surface. Enameled steel and cast iron have different weight and feel characteristics. A heavier tub needs careful consideration of delivery access and floor support. We can compare options with the bathroom conditions and your preferences.

The wall area around the tub matters, too. Choices may include tile or a compatible panel surround. Tile allows flexibility in pattern and grout color. Panels offer a more continuous surface with fewer grout joints. We help coordinate the tub, wall finish, fixtures, and edge details so they work as one assembly.

The existing faucet location may be retained if the plumbing layout allows, or the project can include a different fixture arrangement as part of a wider remodel. In bathrooms with hard municipal or well water, mineral deposits can collect on fixtures and surfaces. Consider cleaning and upkeep when choosing finishes, and follow product care instructions.

If the tub is one part of a larger update, explore our bathroom remodeling service. We can discuss how the tub area will work with shower features and other bathroom finishes.

When replacement makes sense

A tub may need replacement when it is cracked, visibly worn, difficult to clean, or no longer suits the household. Persistent leaks, soft or damaged material around the tub, and signs of water behind the surround call for attention. The source and extent of moisture should be assessed before new finishes cover the area.

Replacement can also make sense during a bathroom refresh when the tub is the feature that no longer works. A different depth, shape, or configuration may better support your routine. If you are updating the room more broadly, it helps to coordinate the tub with flooring, wall finishes, ventilation, and storage.

Freeze-thaw winters are part of life in northern Illinois, although the tub itself is indoors. Local weather can matter when maintaining a home and protecting plumbing in colder areas. For a bathroom project, the key details are sound plumbing connections, suitable water protection, and well-finished transitions around the tub.

The tub or surrounding wall has damage, staining, or recurring moisture concerns.
The current size or configuration is uncomfortable or inconvenient.
You want a tub-to-shower conversion or a coordinated bathroom update.

Local planning, permits, and project coordination

Permit requirements depend on the project scope and the authority serving the property. Work that changes plumbing or other regulated components may require permits and inspections. A straightforward fixture replacement can have different requirements. We review the planned work and handle required permits before construction proceeds.

Libertyville and Mundelein are among the Lake County communities where homeowners should confirm the process for their property. Local requirements can vary, so we do not assume one application or inspection process applies everywhere. Read about our approach to building permits. Lake County also provides general information about building permits.

A clear scope helps everyone understand what is included. We discuss which surfaces are part of the project, how the tub meets the walls, whether existing plumbing stays, and which selections need to be finalized before installation. If an inspection is required, it must be coordinated with the relevant authority and the work sequence.

Rohrer is a family-owned contractor serving Lake County since 1989. We work with homeowners in Vernon Hills and Mettawa and bring local project coordination and permit handling to the job. Learn more about Rohrer for Construction.

A replacement planned as a whole

Installing a new tub involves more than fitting it into the opening. When the old unit is removed, the exposed subfloor and surrounding framing can be checked. The plumbing needs to suit the selected tub, and the wall system needs appropriate water protection. Access to the bathroom and protection for nearby areas are also part of planning the work.

We discuss whether the project will keep the existing footprint or change the room’s arrangement. A new tub and surround can refresh the bathroom while preserving its basic layout. If you want a larger change, we can coordinate tub work with a broader remodel rather than leave adjoining finishes disconnected.

Our process starts with the bathroom and your goals. We review the existing conditions, plan the scope and selections, address required permits, and prepare the work area before installation. After setting the tub and completing the specified finishes, we review the finished scope with you.

Call Rohrer for Construction at 847-668-7183 or request a free estimate through our contact page. Tell us whether you want to replace a tub, update its surround, or consider a shower conversion.

Bathtub Replacement Timeline

A bathtub replacement timeline depends on the selected materials and the work involved. These ranges are planning estimates, not promises; the project scope and any permit needs are assessed during planning.

Consultation and scope
1–2 weeks

Discuss the existing bathroom, the replacement goals and possible layout changes. The team can review design options and identify factors that may affect the work.

Selections and planning
1–3 weeks

Choose materials and fixtures, then develop the project plan. If the scope involves plumbing, electrical or structural changes, assess applicable local permit requirements before construction.

Removal and preparation
1–2 weeks

Remove the existing bathtub and prepare the work area for the replacement. The amount of preparation can vary with the bathroom’s condition and the project scope.

Installation and completion
1–3 weeks

Install the selected bathtub and complete the planned work. The timeline can vary based on materials, layout changes and any additional plumbing or electrical work.

Our bathtub replacement process

We begin by learning what is not working and what you want the bathroom to do. Then we define the project scope, selections, and approvals before installation begins.

01
1. Review the bathroom

We discuss the tub’s condition, how you use the room, and whether you want a replacement, a different layout, or a walk-in shower. We review dimensions, access, adjoining finishes, and visible plumbing conditions.

02
2. Plan the scope and selections

We confirm the work area and discuss tub material, size, surround or tile, and fixtures. If you are updating other parts of the bathroom, we coordinate those elements in the plan.

03
3. Address permits and preparation

We determine whether the planned work requires permits and handle required applications. Before removal, we plan access and prepare to protect the surrounding work area.

04
4. Remove and install

We remove the existing tub and prepare the opening. The replacement is fitted to the planned plumbing and support conditions, then the surround or wall finish is installed.

05
5. Finish and review

We complete the specified trim and finish work, check installed components, and review the project scope with you. Any required inspections are coordinated as part of the work.

Plan the right kind of tub update

Your goals help determine whether a focused replacement or a wider remodel is the right fit.

Replace the existing tub

Keep the familiar bathing function with a new tub. This option suits homeowners who want a refreshed fixture while retaining the room’s general arrangement.

Update the tub and surround

Coordinate a new tub with tile or a panel surround for a complete tub-area update. Consider appearance, cleaning, and how the edges will be finished.

Convert the tub to a shower

Change the room’s function with a walk-in shower in place of the tub. Plan for drainage, water protection, the shower base, and enclosure style.

Tub-to-Shower Conversion in Lake County, IL

Replace an underused bathtub with a shower planned around your bathroom, daily routine, and home. Rohrer for Construction is a family-owned Lake County general contractor serving the area since 1989. We plan the work, coordinate the details, and help homeowners understand permit requirements before construction begins.

Discuss Your Bathroom Project
See Our Projects
Written by Rohrer for Construction | Serving Lake County, IL since 1989 —
Last reviewed/Updated: October 2026
Make the existing bathroom work harder

A tub-to-shower conversion can make a bathroom easier to use without changing the room’s overall footprint. Start by reviewing the tub, surrounding walls, plumbing locations, floor, and available clearance. Keeping fixtures near their current locations may limit plumbing work, while a different shower layout can add complexity.

Many Lake County homes built from the 1950s through the 1990s have ranch, split-level, or colonial layouts with bathrooms sized for a standard tub. A useful plan makes the most of the existing space rather than assuming a larger bathroom is necessary. We discuss layout, materials, and project scope through our bathroom remodeling services.

Measure the shower area and the route into the bathroom.
Review plumbing and visible finishes.
Choose a layout that suits the room and its users.
Choose shower details for comfort and upkeep

A conversion is a chance to decide what belongs in the shower, not just which tub comes out. Depending on the layout and products, options can include a low-threshold entry, built-in niche, handheld showerhead, bench or fold-down seat, and grab bars. Consider these choices together: a seat needs usable clearance, storage should be reachable, and grab bars need appropriate backing and placement.

Tile offers flexibility in color and pattern, while manufactured wall systems can reduce grout joints that need regular cleaning. Floor material, grout, hardware, and glass also affect daily maintenance. Lake County homes may have municipal water or private wells, and water mineral content can contribute to deposits on glass and fixtures. Check cleaning requirements for the products you are considering.

Northern Illinois freeze-thaw winters make reliable indoor moisture management important year-round. A properly planned shower assembly helps manage routine moisture; finish materials alone are not a substitute for a correctly installed waterproofing system.

Compare shower floors for slip resistance and cleaning needs.
Plan niches, seats, and grab bars before selecting wall finishes.
Choose glass and hardware with maintenance in mind.
Understand permits, plumbing, and the work area

Permit requirements depend on project scope and the jurisdiction responsible for the property. Bathroom work in Lake County may involve a village or city building department; Gurnee and Lindenhurst, for example, have local permit processes. Changes to plumbing, electrical, or structural components commonly trigger permit requirements. A finish update may be treated differently, so confirm the rules for your address and proposed work before construction starts.

Rohrer handles necessary permit applications as part of its planning process when the project requires them. We identify the proposed work and coordinate appropriate documentation and approvals before construction. For practical guidance, read our remodeling permit information and confirm local requirements with the authority having jurisdiction.

Ask which department reviews permits for your address.
Clarify whether plumbing, electrical, or structural changes are included.
Include permit and inspection requirements in the project plan.
Plan for the home you have

Older bathrooms can hold surprises behind the tub surround or beneath the floor. The substrate’s condition, previous repairs, and existing plumbing locations can affect the work required after demolition. A reliable scope distinguishes confirmed selections from conditions that cannot be assessed until materials are opened.

A shower can also change how a shared bathroom serves the household. In a ranch, split-level, or colonial, consider who uses the room and whether another bathtub remains available elsewhere. A walk-in shower may suit everyday access, while retaining a tub in a family bathroom may better meet household needs. We can discuss these tradeoffs as part of broader remodeling project planning.

Consider how the household uses this bathroom.
Decide which fixtures and accessories matter most.
Allow time to review concealed conditions found during demolition.
Set expectations for schedule and cost

There is no single timeline for every tub-to-shower conversion. The schedule depends on the work area, material selections and availability, permit or inspection requirements, plumbing changes, and conditions discovered during construction. A straightforward replacement with limited layout changes differs from work that relocates plumbing or requires repairs behind the existing tub. Your project plan should explain the sequence and identify decisions to make before construction begins.

Tub-to-shower conversion cost is shaped by the same scope choices. Keeping plumbing in place can reduce rework compared with moving fixtures, while tile, glass, built-in features, and concealed repairs affect the total. Rohrer’s site notes that moving or reconfiguring bathroom fixtures can require additional labor, plumbing, electrical work, and permitting. An estimate should be based on your room and selections, not a generic online figure. To outline the work, use the home remodeling scope builder.

Confirm what demolition, preparation, installation, and finish work include.
Ask how permits and inspections affect the sequence.
Review material selections alongside the project scope.
A clear process from first discussion to finish

A defined sequence helps homeowners see which decisions come first and how the work moves forward.

01
Discuss the bathroom

Describe what is not working, who uses the space, and the shower features you want. The existing room and plumbing help frame practical options.

02
Review scope and selections

Confirm the proposed layout, materials, fixtures, and changes to plumbing or other systems. A clear scope explains what is included.

03
Plan permits and preparation

When permits apply, coordinate the application and approvals with the appropriate local building department before the related work proceeds.

Complete construction

Curbless Shower Installation

BATHROOM REMODELING IN LAKE COUNTY, ILLINOIS

Curbless Shower Installation

A curbless shower removes the raised threshold between the bathroom floor and shower, creating a cleaner transition and easier access. Rohrer for Construction plans and builds curbless showers as part of a bathroom remodel, coordinating the floor, drain, waterproofing, tile, glass and plumbing as one project. We are a family-owned local contractor serving Lake County since 1989. Request a free estimate to discuss your bathroom and the work needed to make a curbless design practical.

Free Estimate
See Our Projects
Written by Rohrer for Construction | Serving Lake County, IL since 1989 —
Last reviewed/Updated: October 2026
What a curbless shower includes

A curbless shower has no raised curb to step over. Its floor is set up to direct water toward a drain while keeping the bathroom floor outside the shower protected. The finished result depends on more than tile: the shower base, waterproofing, drain location, floor height and enclosure must work together.

The scope can include removing an existing tub or shower, adjusting plumbing, preparing or modifying the floor, installing a waterproofing system, setting tile, fitting glass and installing new fixtures. If the project is part of a broader bathroom remodeling project, we can also plan the shower alongside the vanity, lighting and other room finishes.

Before design decisions are final, we assess the existing floor and drain route. Some bathrooms can accommodate a recessed shower area; others need a different floor or drain plan. In older homes, the available framing depth and existing plumbing can affect what is feasible. A site review helps identify those constraints before materials are selected.

A carefully sloped shower floor that directs water to the drain
A waterproofed shower assembly, including vulnerable transitions
Drain, fixture and glass choices coordinated with the layout
Tile installation and finishing around the shower opening
Choose materials and details for daily use

Tile selection affects appearance, cleaning and footing. Porcelain is a common choice for shower floors and walls because it is available in many formats and finishes. Smaller mosaic pieces can follow a sloped floor more readily and provide more grout lines underfoot; larger wall tile can create a simpler visual pattern. Natural stone is another option, but it may call for more attention to sealing and routine care.

A point drain is typically placed within the shower floor, while a linear drain can sit along an edge or wall when the layout supports it. The drain choice influences how the floor is shaped and where cuts in the tile fall. Grout color, trim, niche placement and shower controls should be considered at the same time so the finished surfaces look intentional and are practical to maintain.

Glass can keep the bathroom feeling open, while a fixed panel or door configuration helps contain spray. Handheld showerheads and well-positioned controls can make the space more convenient. Grab bars can be included in the design, with blocking planned behind the finished wall where needed. A curbless shower alone does not guarantee accessibility; clearances, controls, support and the rest of the bathroom layout matter too.

Porcelain, ceramic or natural-stone tile, selected for the intended use
Mosaic or larger-format tile suited to the floor layout
Point or linear drain, based on the room and slope plan
Glass enclosure, handheld showerhead, niche and optional support bars
Curbless Shower Installation Options

Planning a bathroom remodel in Lake Forest? Compare shower approaches and discuss layout and material choices with Rohrer for Construction.

 	Curbless shower	Curb-entry shower	Shower layout reconfiguration
Best for	Homeowners considering a shower without a raised entry curb	Homeowners keeping a shower with a curb	Homeowners considering a different shower location or layout
What it addresses	A shower entry design choice	A shower entry design choice	Changes to the shower’s position or arrangement
Typical scope of work	Bathroom design and material selections for a curbless shower	Bathroom design and material selections for a curb-entry shower	Layout planning; moving or reconfiguring a shower can involve additional plumbing work
Disruption to the home	Depends on the bathroom plan and selected materials	Depends on the bathroom plan and selected materials	Moving or reconfiguring the shower typically involves more work
When to consider	When exploring a curbless entry as part of a bathroom remodel	When retaining a shower with a curb fits the planned bathroom	When the existing shower location does not fit the desired layout
When a curbless shower may be a good fit

Homeowners often consider a curbless shower when replacing a tub, updating an aging bathroom or making entry easier for someone who finds a high step difficult. It can also suit a bathroom where a low-profile, open shower is a design priority. Think about who uses the room, how much splash containment you need, and whether the shower can fit without compromising other bathroom functions.

Many Lake County homes built from the 1950s through the 1990s—including ranches, split-levels and colonials—have bathroom layouts and floor assemblies that were not designed around a curbless shower. The existing plumbing and framing may limit how the shower floor can be lowered. A successful plan accounts for those conditions rather than assuming the new shower can simply replace the old base.

Freeze-thaw winters make a dry, usable bathroom especially important, but they do not change the need for sound shower detailing. Water must be directed into the drain and kept within the waterproofed area. If your home has hard water, mineral deposits may show on glass and fixtures, so choose finishes with cleaning and upkeep in mind. We can review these considerations during an estimate visit.

Replacing a tub or raised shower threshold
Improving access for changing mobility needs
Updating an older bathroom while keeping the room’s layout workable
Local planning, permits and inspections

A shower remodel that changes plumbing, electrical work or other regulated components may require a permit. Requirements depend on the property’s jurisdiction and project scope; a village may have its own application and inspection process. We review the applicable requirements, prepare and submit permit applications when needed, and coordinate required inspections as part of the project.

Rohrer has served Lake County since 1989 and handles permits for remodeling work. If your home is in Grayslake, the local building department’s process is one part of planning the schedule. We confirm the requirements for the actual project rather than relying on a general assumption. Learn more about our permit process or check the county’s building permit information. You can also learn about Rohrer for Construction and our local experience.

Permit applications are only one part of the preparation. The shower design, material selections and construction plan need to be clear enough to guide the work. Our team discusses the scope with you before construction begins and keeps the project tied to the approved plan.

Review the project scope and the authority responsible for permits
Plan plumbing, floor preparation, waterproofing and finish details together
Coordinate required applications and inspections
Curbless Shower Installation Timeline

A curbless shower project typically moves from planning and material selection through construction and final checks. The ranges below are planning estimates, not guarantees; the actual timeline depends on the design, project scope and any applicable permit process.

Design and project planning
1–2 weeks

Discuss the shower layout, materials and project scope. The team can help review options such as tile and Schluter waterproofing systems.

Plans and permit coordination
1–3 weeks

Once the design is finalized, plans and material specifications are developed. If permits apply to the work, the process includes preparing applications and coordinating with the local building department before construction begins.

Shower construction
1–3 weeks

The existing shower area is prepared and the new curbless shower is built. Changes to plumbing or other parts of the bathroom can affect the work involved and the timeline.

Finishing and final checks
3–7 days

Complete the selected finishes and review the finished work. If the project requires inspections, their timing may affect completion.

Our curbless shower installation process

We start by understanding the bathroom as it exists, then plan the shower around the home, the way you use the space and the work required to build it.

01
1. Visit and discuss your goals

We look at the current shower or tub, bathroom dimensions, access, plumbing and visible floor conditions. You can share priorities such as easier entry, a particular tile style, storage or new fixtures.

02
2. Develop the layout and scope

We determine whether the floor can support a curbless design and discuss drain placement, floor slope, enclosure, tile and fixture options. If the existing conditions call for a different approach, we explain the practical choices.

03
3. Select materials and handle permits

We confirm the project details and selections, prepare the construction plan and handle applicable permit applications. Local review and inspections are coordinated according to the requirements for the property and work.

04
4. Build and finish the shower

The team completes demolition and necessary preparation, then installs the planned shower components, waterproofing, tile, fixtures and glass. We coordinate the work so the drain, floor and enclosure fit the finished design.

05
5. Review the completed work

We review the finished project with you, explain care considerations for the selected materials and address any remaining project items.

Plan the details before construction

A good design balances access, water control and the look you want.

Floor and drain

The shower floor needs a deliberate slope to the drain. Floor height and existing framing help determine the workable design.

Waterproofing

A curbless opening needs careful detailing at the shower floor, walls and transitions to keep water within the intended area.

Tile and upkeep

Choose floor tile suited to the slope and intended use. Consider grout, stone care and hard-water deposits when comparing finishes.

Access and enclosure

Plan glass, controls, storage and optional grab bars around the people using the bathroom and the space available.

A kitchen should support the way your household actually lives. It should feel practical, organized, easy to use, and visually connected to the rest of the home. At Rohrer for Construction, we help homeowners throughout Lake County transform outdated kitchens into modern, functional spaces built around better layouts, smarter storage, quality finishes, and long-term daily usability.

Kitchen Remodel Contractor Services for Lake County Homes

The kitchen is one of the most used spaces in the home. It is where meals are prepared, daily routines overlap, conversations happen, and family life tends to gather. When the layout is awkward, storage is limited, finishes are worn, or the room simply feels outdated, the entire home can feel less functional.

A well-planned kitchen remodel gives homeowners the chance to improve more than just the look of the space. It can make cooking easier, improve traffic flow, create more usable work surfaces, increase storage, and better connect the kitchen to the rest of the home. The goal is not just a prettier room. The goal is a room that works better every day.

Many kitchen remodeling clients also end up exploring bathroom remodeling, basement renovation, or broader general contractor services as part of improving the home as a whole.

What a Kitchen Remodel Can Improve
Better layout and easier movement through the room
Improved cabinet storage and pantry organization
More efficient countertop and prep space
Updated flooring, backsplash, and finish selections
Improved lighting and appliance placement
Cleaner visual flow with the rest of the home
More functional islands and seating areas
Stronger resale appeal and long-term value
Types of Kitchen Remodeling Projects We Handle
Full Kitchen Renovations

A full kitchen renovation is ideal when the room needs a major refresh in layout, finishes, cabinets, countertops, lighting, and overall function. These projects give homeowners the chance to rethink the space from the ground up.

Kitchen Layout Improvements

Some kitchens look acceptable on the surface but still function poorly. Layout-focused remodeling can improve work flow, increase usable prep space, and create a better relationship between cooking, storage, and seating areas.

Small Kitchen Remodeling

Smaller kitchens often require the smartest planning. Better cabinet design, efficient layouts, improved lighting, and strategic storage can make compact kitchens feel more capable without needing extra square footage.

Open Concept Kitchen Updates

When homeowners want the kitchen to feel more open and connected to nearby living or dining space, remodeling can help create a cleaner and more inviting flow throughout the main level of the home.

Popular Kitchen Remodeling Upgrades
Cabinetry, Storage, and Organization

Storage is one of the biggest reasons homeowners remodel a kitchen. Cabinet layout, pantry solutions, drawer systems, and island storage all affect how well the room works. Better cabinetry planning can reduce clutter, improve access, and make the room more enjoyable to use every day.

A kitchen should not force you to work around poor storage decisions. It should support the way you cook, clean, gather, and live.

Countertops, Surfaces, and Finishes

Countertops, flooring, backsplashes, and finish selections shape both the appearance and practicality of the kitchen. The right materials should feel cohesive with the home while also standing up to real daily wear.

A successful remodel balances style with durability. Homeowners should not have to choose between a kitchen that looks good and a kitchen that performs well.

How Kitchen Remodeling Impacts Cost

Kitchen remodeling costs vary based on the size of the room, the complexity of the project, the material selections, and whether the remodel includes layout changes, electrical work, plumbing adjustments, or appliance repositioning. Keeping the general footprint similar is usually more straightforward than redesigning the entire room.

The more moving parts a project has, the more important planning becomes. That is why scope, material choices, and realistic budgeting should be clarified early.

If you are in the planning stage, it may help to review our Kitchen Remodeling Cost Estimator, browse the Advice Center, or review Remodel Financing Options for Lake County homeowners.

Some kitchen projects may also require permit coordination depending on the work involved, and our Building Permits Made Easy resources can help explain what to expect.

Our Kitchen Remodeling Process
01
Consultation

We start by learning about your kitchen, your goals, your layout frustrations, and the kind of finished result you want from the remodel.

02
Planning

Layout direction, cabinet planning, finish selections, budgeting, and any permit-related considerations are organized before construction begins.

03
Construction

Once the scope and selections are set, the project moves into execution with a focus on craftsmanship, detail, and communication.

04
Final Walkthrough

We review the completed kitchen together and make sure the finished space aligns with the original plan and expectations.

Designed for Everyday Life, Not Just Showrooms
A Better Kitchen Should Feel Better to Use

A kitchen can have beautiful finishes and still be frustrating if the layout, storage, lighting, and appliance placement are not planned well. The best kitchen remodels improve both form and function so the room feels more useful every single day.

That is why kitchen remodeling should consider more than cabinets and countertops. Traffic flow, work surfaces, seating, organization, and how the room connects to nearby living space all matter.

If you are still comparing options, you can browse Home Remodeling FAQs, explore Our Work, or read Our Reviews to get a better feel for the process.
